content:
Dear Tessel Cargo Software hiring team,

I’m applying for the Backend Engineer (Python) role on the Routing & Tracking team. I bring more than five years of professional backend experience with Java and Kotlin, and I’m keen to apply that foundation in a role working mainly in Python. My Python experience so far is scripting and small Jenkins helpers, rather than production services.

At Tejo Insurance Tech, I build and support Spring Boot services using PostgreSQL, Kafka and Kubernetes on AWS. I designed a versioned OpenAPI 3 quoting API used by 12 broker partners for around 400,000 requests per month, and improved its safeguards with per-partner rate limiting and contract tests. I also resolved duplicate claim records caused by at-least-once Kafka delivery by implementing a transactional outbox and idempotency keys; duplicates fell from around 40 per week to zero over the following quarter.

Reliable production systems and clear communication are important parts of my work. I take part in a monthly on-call rota, handled a major Kafka lag incident, and wrote a follow-up that was praised. Earlier, at Viajar Online, I raised payments-module test coverage from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers and extracted notifications from a Java monolith into a separate Spring Boot service. These experiences align with Tessel’s focus on dependable services, ownership and concise technical communication.

I’m interested in bringing my API, event-processing and production-support experience to Tessel’s shipment-tracking platform while developing further as a Python backend engineer. Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience could contribute to the Routing & Tracking team.

Best regards,
Daniel Okafor-Reyes

critique.content_quality_feedback: The cover letter is clear, professional, well structured, and appropriately concise. It uses strong quantified evidence: 12 broker partners, approximately 400,000 requests per month, and duplicate claims reduced from around 40 per week to zero. The examples demonstrate API design, event-processing reliability, automated testing, incident response, and service extraction. The tone is honest about the candidate’s current Python level, which supports credibility. The main weakness is that the opening frames Python primarily as a limitation rather than presenting Java/Kotlin as the comparable backend experience explicitly accepted by the advertisement.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The letter is ATS-friendly: it uses standard paragraphs, no complex formatting, tables, graphics, headers, or unusual section labels. It includes several relevant terms such as Java, Kotlin, Python, Spring Boot, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, AWS, OpenAPI 3, contract tests, Testcontainers, transactional outbox, and idempotency keys. It does not explicitly use some supported job-ad terminology, including REST APIs, Docker, automated testing, and CI/CD. Adding only the supported terms would improve keyword matching without overstating the candidate’s experience. FastAPI, GitHub Actions, query tuning, schema migrations, and observability tools should not be added because they are not supported by the candidate information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The letter aligns strongly with the role’s comparable-language requirement: the candidate has more than five years of professional Java/Kotlin backend experience and expresses interest in working mainly in Python. It also matches the team’s emphasis on dependable services, event processing, production support, technical communication, Kafka, Kubernetes, AWS, APIs, and automated testing. The on-call incident and follow-up write-up are particularly relevant to the role’s incident-response and post-mortem responsibilities. The candidate material does not establish query tuning or safe live-data schema migrations, so that part of the PostgreSQL requirement remains a gap. Python production-service experience, FastAPI, GitHub Actions, observability tooling, logistics or EDI knowledge, and Dutch/French language skills are also not demonstrated. These are candidate-profile gaps rather than defects that can be solved through rewriting.
critique.improvement_instructions:
1. In the opening paragraph, replace the sentence "My Python experience so far is scripting and small Jenkins helpers, rather than production services" with a more positively framed but still truthful version: "My professional backend experience is in Java and Kotlin, which the role explicitly recognises as comparable experience, and I am keen to work mainly in Python; my Python experience to date includes data-fix scripts and small Jenkins helpers." This preserves transparency while leading with the relevant qualification.

2. In the second paragraph, change "I build and support Spring Boot services using PostgreSQL, Kafka and Kubernetes on AWS" to "I build and support Java and Kotlin Spring Boot REST API services using PostgreSQL, Kafka and Kubernetes on AWS." This adds the supported terms "Java," "Kotlin," and "REST API" in language closer to the advertisement.

3. In the third paragraph, revise the Viajar Online sentence to include the supported Docker and automated-testing keywords: "Earlier, at Viajar Online, I raised automated test coverage in the payments module from 35% to 70% using Testcontainers and extracted notifications from a Java monolith into a separate Spring Boot service using RabbitMQ and Docker." Do not describe this as GitHub Actions or claim ownership of a CI/CD pipeline.

4. In the final paragraph, replace "my API, event-processing and production-support experience" with "my REST API, Kafka event-processing, automated-testing and production-support experience." This more directly mirrors the role’s terminology while remaining supported by the candidate’s documented experience.
